title: Outdoor Comfort Score Seasonal Baseline Drift
dataSources: Weather-station readings (`weatherstation:reading`), daily weather-impact rollups (`personalweather:daily`), sleep correlation records (`personalweather:sleep`), step correlation records (`personalweather:steps`), mood correlation records (`personalweather:mood`).
app: Local weather-station readings correlated with personal sleep, steps, mood, and outdoor-activity summaries in Splunk via scripted inputs and daily rollups.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=personalweather:daily
| stats avg(outdoor_comfort_score) as avg_metric by season
| eventstats avg(avg_metric) as overall_avg
| eval delta=round(avg_metric-overall_avg,2)
| sort - delta
description: Compares seasonal averages for outdoor comfort score against your overall norm so slow weather-linked drift becomes visible.
value: Seasonal drift is where long, subtle weather effects show up even when daily correlation looks weak.
implementation: Write a season label onto each daily record during ingest for easier quarterly review.
visualization: Bar chart of seasonal average outdoor comfort score versus overall baseline.
grandmaExplanation: It produces whether one season tends to push your outdoor comfort score noticeably up or down.
